rubric: Evaluate this synthetic computer-voice reproduction experiment by LISTENING. The reference is the target timbre and delivery. Candidate labels are randomized; no model identity or latency is supplied. Do not identify the speaker. For each candidate transcribe what you actually hear before grading. Separate intelligibility from voice fidelity. Score 0-100 for timbre, pitch/prosody, robotic articulation, continuity (clicks, splices, missing phonemes), and text accuracy versus its requested text. Voice fidelity: 100 identical recording, 95 virtually indistinguishable, 90 clearly same style with small audible differences, 75 similar computer voice but visibly/audibly different synthesizer, 50 generic robot voice with substantial mismatch, 25 unrelated voice. Do not award high fidelity merely for sounding robotic. A different requested name or sentence is intentional, not a fidelity error. Compare pitch/pace/style to reference; rhythm need not be identical for different text. Record concrete audible differences. For personalized phrases especially inspect the name's pronunciation and transitions into and out of it; score name_seam_quality (null for lines without a personalized name). Return JSON {candidates:[{id,transcript,timbre,pitch_prosody,robotic_articulation,continuity,text_accuracy,voice_fidelity,name_seam_quality,observations}]}. These subjective scores will be reviewed by a human; do not imply calibrated accuracy.
notes: Two blinded, independently ordered judgments per sample. Latency and model names withheld. Not a calibrated perceptual percentage. Independent prompts, not independent model families.
